about.title: About Me
about.intro: My specialty: turning scattered operational data into reliable, decision-ready information.
description: I'm an AI Data Engineer with 3+ years across data engineering, analytics and software engineering. At Instituto Semear, I built a People Analytics platform in Python and Streamlit that brought 10,000+ scholarship applications from 5 years into one place, automating cleaning, transformation and executive reporting.

My software engineering background (Go, Java/Spring Boot, TypeScript, Docker, CI/CD, AWS) means I can take a data solution from ingestion all the way to production, and my experience with requirements and agile teams helps make sure it answers the right business question.

items.title: Football Recruitment Analytics
items.subtitle: Scouting app on open data with a player value model
items.description: A bilingual (EN/PT) Streamlit scouting app on open data covering 8 leagues and 3 seasons (6,782 players, 6,260 league games), built for clubs that recruit on a tight budget and need to explain every decision to the sporting director. Every number shows how much evidence is behind it.
items.problem: Clubs with small budgets have to spot value early, often in leagues others watch less, and justify each signing with data.
approach: Data pipeline: checksum-pinned download, DuckDB extraction to Parquet and 14 automated data checks; goal events match the final score in 6,255 of 6,260 games
Player metrics: per-90 and on-pitch numbers as percentiles against same-position peers, with confidence labels based on minutes played
Value model: regression of market value on output, age and league strength (R² 0.65–0.75), backtested on past seasons
Scouting workflow: similar-player search, side-by-side shortlist and a one-page report per player

items.title: Floripa na Praia
items.subtitle: Full-stack civic-tech platform (capstone project)
items.description: Full-stack civic-tech platform built in Java with Spring Boot (MVC) and a React frontend by a 3-person team over 1 year. It lets users report conditions across 42+ beaches in Florianópolis, sized for summer demand of up to 800,000 beachgoers.
items.problem: Beachgoers had no single, up-to-date source on beach conditions during the city's peak tourism season.
approach: 6 months of requirements research, validating the concept with 150+ users before development
Google Maps API for geolocation and the OpenAI API for a generative AI feature that triages incident reports
Relational PostgreSQL model and an automated test suite (80%+ coverage) with Selenium end-to-end tests, in a CI/CD pipeline for cloud deployment
items.impact: 70,000 concurrent users validated in load tests

items.title: People Analytics System for Selection Process
items.subtitle: Automated Analysis and Diversity Indicators
items.description: Five years of scholarship applications (12,000+ candidates, 2022 to 2026) were spread across spreadsheets and forms. I built a Streamlit analytics platform that answers the team's key questions on fairness, reach, conversion and evaluation quality.
items.problem: No way to evaluate the selection process as a whole: data from 5 editions scattered across spreadsheets and forms, with no view of conversion, bias or evaluation consistency.
approach: Data pipeline with automated cleaning, deduplication and consolidation of 5 editions, with built-in quality checks that flagged 928 duplicate submissions
Funnel analysis across every stage (application → group dynamic → interview → approval), finding the main bottleneck: only 22.9% of applicants reached the group dynamic
Fairness metrics: a representativeness index comparing approved vs. applicant profiles across demographic groups
Evaluation consistency: score distributions per criterion, correlation between stages and outlier detection across 75 evaluators
Auto-generated executive summary with confidence labels on each insight
items.impact: 12,000+ applications from 5 editions analyzed in one place
